title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 2) Bill 2026
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 2) Bill 2026

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would introduce refundable loss carry back offsets, permanently extend the small business instant asset write-off, and exempt specified Papua New Guinea (PNG) rugby employment income.
Eligible corporate tax entities, excluding significant global entities, could offset revenue losses against tax paid in either or both of the two preceding income years.
From 1 July 2026, businesses with aggregated annual turnover below $10 million could immediately deduct eligible assets costing less than $20,000 when first used or installed.
changes: The loss carry back measure would apply to income years beginning on or after 1 July 2026.
Offsets would be limited by earlier tax liabilities and generally by the entity's available franking balance.
Capital losses would be ineligible for carry back.
The PNG Chiefs Limited employment income exemption would cover the 2025-26 income year and the following nine income years.
summary.affected: Eligible corporate tax entities, small businesses and people deriving income from PNG Chiefs Limited employment are affected.

speeches.speaker: Tony Sheldon
speeches.brief: Presented the Selection of Bills Committee's seventh report and moved its adoption; the report recommended immediate referral of four bills concerning defence, health insurance and tax reform to Senate committees with reporting dates from 13 August to 7 October 2026, while an amendment proposed referring a workplace relations bill by 10 August.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Moved a successful motion to amend the sitting schedule so the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 2) Bill 2026 and the News Journalism Payments Bill 2026 and related bills would be debated later that day, with priority extending until 10 pm if needed.
